newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end at another yearly high of 756.77.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end at another yearly high of 756.77.

text.p: Stocks closed at another yearly high on Saturday as investors continued to believe in a coming economic turnaround and falling interest rates, brokers said.
They said better-than-expected macroeconomic indicators also boosted investor hopes for an economic recovery.
The composite stock index stood at 756.77 at the close, up 10.41 points from Friday. Advancing issues swamped decliners by 451 to 299.
Traders said rumours that Hanshin Construction Co would default on loans dampened early morning trading, but that the market shrugged off anxieties and turned around.
Hanshin Construction applied for court receivership on Friday and its main creditor SEOULBANK said it would not extend further credits to the company.
Traders said that the stock market would continue to strengthen early next week but that a downward consolidation was expected for the latter part of the week.
The benchmark three-year corporate bond yields closed at 12.50 percent on Saturday down 0.02 percentage points from Friday's closing.
Volume totalled 38.9 million shares in Saturday's half-day trading session.
